channel.title: The Forge
channel.description: A daily hour. Private curriculum, built for one listener.
channel.itunes:author: Prinz

item.title: [Spiritual Traditions] The Kybalion’s Seven Principles Explained
item.description: The All, mental creation and the seven principles explained through close reading and an original pottery workshop case. Distinguishes the book's metaphysical claims from modest practical adaptations. Five recall questions with answers and a private paper exercise. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Relationships] How to Flirt and Build a Mutual Connection
item.description: Conversation, flirting and dating through original adult exhibition and cafe cases. Learn how to express interest, make clear invitations, adapt to different responses, explore compatibility and recognise pressure. Brief research discussions on liking and responsiveness, plus a clearly labelled comparison with Deida's polarity framework. Five recall questions with answers and a paper dialogue exercise. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Physics] Why the Same Music Sounds Different Around a Room
item.description: Sound explained through speakers, reflections, room modes and musical instruments. Work through frequency, wavelength, pressure, phase, resonance, harmonics and beats using original numerical examples. Five recall questions with answers and a paper room-model exercise. Selected classical acoustics passages checked against modern physics references; no prior physics knowledge required.

item.title: [History] How Augustus Ruled Rome Without Calling Himself King
item.description: How Augustus combined provincial military command, public powers, money and prestige while republican offices survived. Explains the settlements of 27 and 23 BCE, veterans, public works and succession. Includes five recall questions with answers and a historical power-map exercise. Based on selected passages from Polybius, Augustus and Cassius Dio, with museum context. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Creativity] How Stories Build Tension and Meaning
item.description: Build an original music-box story through consequential choices, viewpoint, dialogue, scene and summary, and an earned ending. Includes contrasting drafts, five recall questions with answers, and a short scene-writing exercise. Craft references: selected sections of Aristotle's Poetics and Edith Wharton's The Writing of Fiction. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Applied Practice] Make the Job Work: Time, Cash and Clear Agreements
item.description: Sunday application of the published September 14 habits, September 15 cash-flow and September 16 negotiation lessons. Work through an original print-studio project from enquiry to payment, then contrast a family keepsake project. Five recall questions with answers and a fictional one-page planning exercise. No prior reading required.

item.title: [Persuasion] Why Favours, Crowds and Scarcity Change Decisions
item.description: Reciprocity, social proof and scarcity explained through research and original workshop examples. Covers useful samples, relevant testimonials, real availability, decision-making and measured outcomes. Five recall questions with answers and a fictional invitation exercise. No prior reading required.

item.title: [AI & Technology] How Language Models Turn Words into Answers
item.description: Inside a language model: tokens, embeddings, attention, training, sampling, context, retrieval and tool use. Original numerical examples and a fictional cafe assistant show how the pieces fit together. Five recall questions with answers and a practical paper exercise. No prior technical knowledge required.

item.title: [Fitness] How Muscles Grow: Training, Recovery and Progress
item.description: Muscle growth explained through two fictional training logs: effort, rest, weekly volume, exercise selection, progression, food, recovery and plateaus. Includes five recall questions with answers and a low-risk exercise for reviewing a training log. General education for healthy adults, not an individual training prescription.

item.title: [Communication] How to Negotiate Without Giving Everything Away
item.description: Prepare alternatives, understand interests, trade across scope and timing, handle pressure, and reach clear agreements. A fictional design project develops into complete worked conversations, with five recall prompts and one practical exercise.

item.title: [Business & Money] Why Profitable Businesses Run Out of Cash
item.description: September 15 catch-up lesson: profit versus cash, contribution and break-even, pricing and discounts, financial statements, inventory, growth funding, and practical cash forecasting. Original worked business cases, five recall questions and one forecast exercise.

item.title: [Psychology] Why You Repeat Habits You Want to Break (Expanded)
item.description: Expanded edition: a full lesson on automatic habits, reinforcement, triggers, friction, practical plans and recovery. Worked cases cover distraction, reading, creative work and business administration. Replaces the original short edition.

item.title: [Critical Thinking] The First Test: How to Know What Helps.
item.description: A foundation for The Forge: evaluate claims, distinguish observation from explanation, and practise with a worked example. Revised edition with clearer dialogue, recall questions and a reading companion approach.

item.title: [Critical Thinking] The Filter
item.description: You own two hundred and forty books and believe almost none of it. That's the correct response, and here's what to do with it.

item.title: [Critical Thinking] Pilot 3: The Filter
item.description: Third pass. Dense, fluent, nothing wasted.

item.title: [Evaluating Books & Beliefs] The Nine
item.description: Segment one, the three piles. Segment two, six books off your own shelf under pressure, including Neville taken seriously. Segment three, the nine, and tonight's ten minutes of work.

item.title: [Critical Thinking] Pilot: The Filter
item.description: Cold open. Two hundred and forty books and the one thing that has to be installed before any of them count.
